[[File:Nesterenko.jpg|thumb|300px|Vassili Nesterenko]]
'''Vassili Nesterenko''' (2 December 1934 – 25 August 2008) was a Soviet and Belarusian physicist from [[Ukraine]] and a former director of the Institute of Nuclear Energy at the [[National Academy of Sciences of Belarus]] (1977–1987).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nasb.gov.by/eng/news/news2009dec.php|title=news|year=2009|publisher=National Academy of Sciences of Belarus|url-status=dead|access-date=6 August 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111217100316/http://nasb.gov.by/eng/news/news2009dec.php|archive-date=17 December 2011}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Vassili Nesterenko (sometimes romanized as Vasilii) was born in Krasny Kut Village, Antratsyt Raion, [[Luhansk Oblast]], Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic (now [[Ukraine]]). He had a diploma from the [[Bauman Moscow State Technical University]]. In 1972 Nesterenko was elected a corresponding member of Academy of Sciences of Byelorussian Soviet Socialistic Republic in the field of Nuclear Power Plants.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nasb.gov.by/eng/members/memoriam/nesterenko.php|publisher=The National Academy of Sciences of Belarus|title=Corresponding Member Vasilii B. NESTERENKO (1934–2008)}}</ref> He worked on the consequences of the [[Chernobyl disaster]].

Since 1990, he had been the director of the Belarusian Independent Institute of "Belrad", created in 1989 with the help of [[Andrei Sakharov]], [[Ales Adamovich]] and [[Anatoly Karpov]].

He attempted to warn the public of the dangerous radiation caused during the Chernobyl explosion. Because of his activities, he lost his job and got problems with the [[State Security Committee of the Republic of Belarus|KGB]].<ref>{{cite journal |first1=ANNE MARIE |last1=MERGIER |title=Crimen Nuclear |journal=Proceso |date=24 April 2016 |url=https://www.proceso.com.mx/438253/crimen-nuclear |access-date=7 June 2019}}</ref>

Vassili Nesterenko died on 25 August 2008 at the age of 73 and was survived by his son.

==Work in Chernobyl==
{{Chernobyl}}
Nesterenko intervened immediately after news of the accident in the nuclear power plant started to spread. As an expert on the subject and with his experience as a fire fighter, he threw [[liquid nitrogen]] containers from a helicopter on the burning reactor core. To do this he had to move into the middle of radioactive smoke. Despite the heavy radioactive contamination of the area, Nesterenko survived. However, of the four passengers of his helicopter, three died from radioactive irradiation and contamination.<ref name="Tchertkoff">''Le Crime de Tchernobyl, le Goulag nucléaire'', de [[Wladimir Tchertkoff]], Actes Sud, avril 2006.</ref>{{page needed|date=January 2016}}

In 1990 Nesterenko founded the Institute of Radiation Safety (BELRAD), which carries out "[[radiation monitoring]] of the inhabitants of Chernobyl zone and their foodstuffs, development of measures on maintenance of radiation safety and protection of the population on territories, contaminated by radionuclides by realization of necessary scientific researches, development and organization of implementation of their results in practice."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.belrad-institute.org/UK/doku.php|title=presentation · UK|publisher=The institute of radiating safety "BELRAD"|access-date=11 March 2015|archive-date=14 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190214083352/http://belrad-institute.org/UK/doku.php|url-status=dead}}</ref>
